b: I was reading a book about Jewish 20th century history, and towards the beginning it gave a very big-picture overview of how Jews were treated in Christian Europe and the Islamic world throughout the Middle Ages. (A pretty imperfect summary based on what I know, but it wasn't the point of the book so that's forgivable.) But afterwards, thinking about it, I realized there was one big region/political entity completely left out. And that it's been normally left out in other things I've read. The Byzantine Empire! So, I know we're talking about a pretty long time period, but can anyone give an overview about Jews and the Jewish community in the Byzantine Empire? Both what kind of a presence they had there and how they were treated.
